Episodic

ep-ih-SOD-ik -- stress on the third syllable, SOD. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Episodic is irregular and occasional; occurring in scattered episodes.

His exercise routine was episodic -- two energetic weeks in January, then nothing at all until spring.

Worked Example

A pen pal writes three long letters in a single month, disappears for half a year, then suddenly writes twice more before going quiet again.

That stop-and-start pattern is episodic: the letters come in irregular, occasional bursts rather than at steady intervals. Something episodic happens in separate episodes with unpredictable gaps between them.

How Episodic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

intermittent

intermittent: stopping and starting at irregular intervals

occasional

occasional: happening now and then, not often

fitful

fitful: coming in irregular, restless bursts

Antonyms

continuous

continuous: unbroken, without interruption

constant

constant: happening all the time without change

How Strong Is It? — occasional → episodic → fitful

occasional vs. episodic

occasional vs. episodic: Occasional is milder than episodic -- it just means 'now and then,' while episodic adds the picture of distinct bursts of activity separated by long, irregular silences.

fitful vs. episodic

fitful vs. episodic: Fitful pushes the irregularity further than episodic: episodic activity comes in identifiable episodes, while fitful suggests restless, broken starts and stops with no shape to them at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — episode

root — episode: an incident or installment; literally 'a coming in besides' (Greek epeisodion, from epi- 'in addition' + eisodos 'way in' (eis 'into' + hodos 'way'))

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Episodic is simply the English word episode plus -ic ('having the characteristics of'). An episode was originally 'a coming in besides' -- an extra scene inserted into a Greek play -- so something episodic behaves like episodes do: it arrives in separate installments with gaps in between.

Use the root in a new word: exodus

Use the root in a new word: exodus: During the heat wave, the city saw a mass exodus to the cooler mountain towns.

Root Check

Word Choice

Think of a television series: it comes in episodes, one at a time, with waits in between. Anything episodic works the same way -- episodic rainfall, episodic interest, episodic chapters in a memoir. The emphasis is on irregular, occasional bursts rather than a steady flow.
